chapter: Early listening, piano and adolescent conflict
title: What counts as jazz, sanctified churches and rock and roll
summary: He says all music is being mixed up and called jazz, traces rock and roll to holy-roller churches, and objects to the old dictionary definition.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: without getting into the controversy of which is best or which is right, this is all part of jazz music, which at this time I would have to truthfully say -- I'd have to go out on a limb and say that it's a lot of controversy about what is good jazz and what is really jazz today.

Because in this period, they are mixing up all kinds of music. They play Latin music, they play what they call rock and roll music, which incidently going back to these early days the sound of rock and roll actually created a avenue,expression for the people who came up in what was known as black community as the holy rolly church. And they had ministers who were unorthodox, without license to preach, who had these large followings of black people, and they did all these dances which were sort of a primitive type, and chants because of this crazy dance. They used to dance, jump up in the air.

We youngsters used to go and see this, it was like going to a carnival to see these people do this, in our way of thinking. Because it was actually -- as far as the church laws, they were not really legal expressions of christianity. But it was an avenue to get to many uneducated people with christianity that wouldn't go to a church more disciplined. And out of this music came what today is known as rock and roll, you see.

Yes. But to get back to my point, they have misconstrued the word jazz at this time by the inclusion of the liberal feeling and concept that all music is jazz or all music is good if it's played good. That's true, but after all you don't play football in a baseball park unless you play and get rid of the bases. You know.
You don't play basketball without the hoop.
Yes, you see. Do you understand what I mean?

So by that reason as I said there still is that struggle. I have it, everybody has it, you know. But the beautiful part about my beginning, and I would like to think my present participation in music, other fields as well as jazz, because I don't consider myself to be just a jazz player. The word means nothing to me except that high feel that the interpretation of the word jazz means not what the original Webster's dictionary said it was. I would like to quote from Webster's dictionary that I read some years ago when I was studying music, that Negro music was considered to be jazz, and they expressed it verbatim as to be loud and boisterous, negroid music. Was considered to be the term for

jazz. You see? So when we think of terms terminology we have to be very careful how we talk about things and how we interpret things because I've been fortunate to live through a couple periods, and that's why it's so difficult for young people to understand the disciplinary measures that were used by the old people and so forth and so on, because there's some things they don't understand, the why's, therefore's and all that you know, which has to do with it, you see.
But I said, it was my desire to express this happiness and the joy and beauty in me that made me decide to be a musician.
